properties.statement:
A MALFORMED TOOL CALL CAN PUT ITS OWN MARKUP INSIDE A DESIGN NODE'S PROSE, AND THE WRITE SUCCEEDS. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-08-23 and REPRODUCED HERE 2026-09-04, by the agent that had read their report earlier the same day.

THEIR REPORT: 'I twice let a closing tag leak into a `decision` parameter (`</decision>` plus a stray `<parameter name="rationale">` landing inside the node text). ENTIRELY MY ERROR, NOT REFLOW2'S — but the write SUCCEEDED both times and the corruption was ONLY VISIBLE ON READING THE ECHOED NODE BACK. A cheap guard would help: reject or warn on a property value containing `<parameter name=` or a stray closing tag matching the parameter's own name, since NEITHER CAN BE LEGITIMATE DESIGN PROSE.'

MY REPRODUCTION, and it is the reason this is recorded as a fact rather than filed as their claim: writing `dec:idea-should-reflow2-ship-a-companion-for-the-file-side-work-it-refuses-to-do`, the `rationale` argument was terminated early and the node was stored with its prose ending:

    ...says nothing about the other.</rationale>
    <parameter name="related_to">[{"relation": "DEPENDS_ON", ...}]

The write returned SUCCESS. The `related_to` links were silently NOT DRAWN — they were stored as literal text in a prose field instead of being interpreted — so the node was both corrupted AND missing the relations the same call was meant to create. Caught only by reading the echoed node back, exactly as they said.

⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT AGENTS, TWELVE DAYS APART, AND THE SECOND ONE HAD READ THE FIRST ONE'S WARNING THAT MORNING. That is the strongest form of evidence for a guard: not that the mistake is easy to make, but that KNOWING ABOUT IT DOES NOT PREVENT IT. It is a harness-level serialization slip, not a reasoning error, so no amount of care by the caller removes it.

⚠️ AND THE SILENT-LOSS HALF IS WORSE THAN THE CORRUPTION HALF. A visibly mangled paragraph gets noticed on the next read. A `related_to` that was never drawn leaves an idea with no neighbours — indistinguishable from an idea nobody linked, which is the exact state `review_relations`' `note` parameter exists to make distinguishable.

THEIR PROPOSED GUARD, which is cheap and specific: reject or warn when a property value contains `<parameter name=` or a closing tag matching the parameter's own name. Neither string can be legitimate design prose. ⭐ IT WOULD ALSO HAVE CAUGHT THE SILENT LOSS, because the giveaway text and the undrawn edges arrive in the same call.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how often this happens unnoticed. Two occurrences are known because two agents read their own writes back; a session that did not would have left the corruption in place, and nothing counts it. The store is a property bag by design, so no schema check would have refused it either.
